canvas-engineering: Research Report

Date: April 2026 | Version: 0.4.2 | Code: github.com/JacobFV/canvas-engineering

What is canvas-engineering?

A typed process compiler for neural architectures. You declare brain regions with typed families (observation, state, memory, residual, action), connect them with a declared topology matching real cortical pathways, and the compiler generates attention masks, loss weights, and scheduling rules. The model doesn't discover what its internal state means — you declare it.

Key finding: Structured cortical topology achieves R²=0.838 on next-timestep cortical dynamics prediction using real TRIBE v2 brain data — outperforming flat MLP baselines when operating at sufficient dimensionality (135 features vs 23 scalars).

3D Brain Surface: Canvas Region Mapping

23 cortical regions from the Destrieux atlas mapped to canvas-engineering regions. Each region gets a typed family (observation for sensory cortex, state for association areas, action for motor cortex) and connects via 42 known cortical pathways.

Experiment 1: Cortical Dynamics Prediction

Task: Given ROI activations at times [t, t+1, t+2], predict activations at t+3. Data: 72 text stimuli processed through Facebook's TRIBE v2 brain encoding model, producing temporal cortical predictions on fsaverage5 (20,484 vertices).

Experiment 2: Brain-Computer Interface

Canvas-structured decoder on real TRIBE v2 cortical predictions. 4 stimulus categories (motor, language, visual, emotion), 32 stimuli total. Virtual EEG sampled via 10-20 electrode patches on fsaverage5.

Canvas decoder (68.8%) vs SVM baseline (59.4%) on real cortical data

Experiment 3: Multi-Robot Fleet Control

4-robot fleet with 51 canvas regions, 189 structured connections. 2D physics simulation with lidar, obstacles, and formation control. Scaling analysis across 2, 4, and 8 robots.

Robot fleet trajectory animation

Next Steps: Foundational Brain World Model

Compute requirement: ~2,000-4,000 GPU-hours on 8xH100 (2-3 weeks wall time).
Train on real fMRI datasets (HCP, NSD, BOLD5000) with ~500 cortical regions, predicting full spatiotemporal activation dynamics across text, audio, and video modalities.
